title: Juniper and the Garden
premise: August Montrose, a mercenary bound to the silent god Vesper, keeps ledgers for the Gilded Root, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, souls. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted, August's own hidden gift of hearing debts marks her as prey, and she discovers the guild sold her sister Juniper's soul to the court beneath the mountain thirteen moons ago. To save Juniper before the moon completes its thirteenth turn, August must betray the guild that raised her, rally a found family of hunted misfits, and confront the truth that her silent god never abandoned her—she did. In the end, August pays her own memories as the price to free Juniper, choosing loyalty over self, and the god speaks at last: not absolution, but an invitation to begin again.
about_author: Ada Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate sales and claims she once bought a ledger no one could account for. She writes fantasy about debt, devotion, and the people we choose, from a house full of plants that refuse to die.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV August. In the Gilded Root's counting room, August balances accounts for bottled grief and borrowed luck while hiding her gift: she hears every debt spoken aloud. A routine entry—a soul, sold thirteen moons past—whispers in a voice she knows. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath competent routine.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: POV August. August traces the entry and finds Juniper's name, her sister lost since childhood, sold by the guild itself to the court beneath the mountain. The moon is one turn from completing its cycle—when the sale becomes permanent. Emotional beat: betrayal cracking open old grief.

chapters.title: The Crown's Proclamation
chapters.summary: POV August. Criers announce a hunt for anyone with the gift; neighbors vanish overnight. The guild master, Corvane, offers August protection—if she surrenders her ledger access and swears new oaths. She realizes he means to make her complicit. Emotional beat: gilded cage closing.

chapters.title: What the God Left Behind
chapters.summary: POV August. August visits the abandoned shrine of Vesper, the god who went silent when she was young, and finds the altar cold but her old votive candle still burning. Someone has been tending it. Emotional beat: aching hope she doesn't trust.

chapters.title: A Thief Named Wren
chapters.summary: POV August. Caught breaking into the guild vault, August collides with Wren, a pickpocket gifted with unluckiness she flings at enemies. Wren recognizes the hunt-mark on August's door and offers alliance instead of alarm. Emotional beat: wary first spark of found family.

chapters.title: The Debt I Hear
chapters.summary: POV August. Interrogated by Corvane about a missing page, August uses her gift to hear his hidden debts—and learns he owes the under-mountain court a debt measured in souls, due when the moon turns. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the enemy has a face.

chapters.title: Bramble and Bone
chapters.summary: POV August. Fleeing the guildhouse, August shelters with Bramble, a hedge-witch healer gifted with growing things, who once treated Juniper's fevers. Bramble confirms the soul-sale's terms and joins them, bringing her garden's secrets. Emotional beat: fragile sanctuary.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: POV August. Crown hunters with iron hounds sweep the city; Wren's bad-luck charm saves them by inches, but Bramble's shop burns. August hears the hunters' leader carrying a debt to Corvane—the guild is feeding names to the crown. Emotional beat: rage hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Songs for the Silent
chapters.summary: POV August. Following the burning votive candle's trail, they find Sable, a blind singer gifted with memory-song, who remembers what August has forgotten: the night Vesper went silent, and August's part in it. Emotional beat: devastating half-truths.

chapters.title: The Night I Stopped Listening
chapters.summary: POV August. Sable sings back August's buried memory: as a child, August begged Vesper to take her pain and, refused, cursed him into silence—her vow broke the god's voice, not his will. Emotional beat: shame, and the first honest reckoning with herself.

chapters.title: Down the Stair That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV August. Guided by Sable's memory-song, the four find the hidden stair beneath the old shrine leading toward the court under the mountain. Each step costs a memory as toll. Emotional beat: sacrifice made literal, bonds tested.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV August. They enter a court of pale nobles who trade in souls like currency, where time pools and moons are counted on bone calendars. August poses as a debt-collector for the Gilded Root. Emotional beat: vertigo and performance under pressure.

chapters.title: Juniper
chapters.summary: POV August. August finds Juniper—alive, serving the court, her soul caged in a lantern but her mind sharp and furious. Juniper refuses rescue framed as another person deciding for her. Emotional beat: reunion laced with resentment and love.

chapters.title: Terms of Sale
chapters.summary: POV August. Reading the contract with her gift, August finds the loophole: the sale voids if a greater debt is paid in the seller's name—but Corvane arrives to collect early, holding Wren hostage. Emotional beat: trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV August. Confronting Corvane in the court, August reads aloud every debt he's hidden, turning the court's own accounting against him until the nobles claim him as payment. Emotional beat: triumphant, terrible justice.

chapters.title: The Price of a Soul
chapters.summary: POV August. The court demands its greater debt: a life's worth of memory, freely given. August steps forward before Juniper can, offering everything she is. Emotional beat: love as deliberate, unflinching cost.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: POV August (fractured). As the moon completes its turn, August pays piece by piece—her name, her vows, her sister's face—while Wren, Bramble, and Sable anchor her with songs, charms, and stubborn hands. Emotional beat: climax; identity dissolving in held hands.

chapters.title: The Lantern Goes Dark
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Freed as the contract burns, Juniper carries the hollowed August up the stair, paying tolls with her own recovered memories to keep her sister walking. Emotional beat: reversal—rescue flowing both ways.

chapters.title: Empty Shrine, Burning Candle
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Above ground, August remembers nothing—not the guild, not the hunt, not herself. At Vesper's shrine, the god finally speaks, offering to restore what she paid. Emotional beat: hushed awe after ruin.

chapters.title: What the God Asks
chapters.summary: POV August. Vesper offers restoration but asks instead that August choose him freely, without debt or desperation—an invitation, not a command. August, blank slate, must decide who to be. Emotional beat: grace offered without strings.

chapters.title: New Ledgers
chapters.summary: POV August. August declines total restoration, keeping only what her found family re-teaches her: Wren's schemes, Bramble's garden, Sable's songs, Juniper's laugh. Together they burn the Gilded Root's soul-ledgers and open something kinder. Emotional beat: rebuilding, chosen family solidified.

chapters.title: The Garden at Month's End
chapters.summary: POV August. One year on, in a garden above the old shrine, August tends plants and a small honest trade in possible things. Juniper plants a tree; Vesper's voice is a warm presence, not a chain. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory reborn as story.
